# s165 — Show the in-work and review queues in one step

Seeing who is on a slice, or what is waiting for review, means naming the configured statuses. In-work is `slicer list --status started --status reviewing`. Ready for review is `slicer list --status review`. The TUI takes the same selection in the filter panel. `reviewing` belongs with in-work, so leaving it out of the review filter is easy to get wrong.

**Findings:** user request: list and the TUI can show these queues only by naming each status · **Size:** M · **Tree:** slicer

**Not in this slice:** a filter by claim owner; pulling sibling-worktree claims into these views; a claim column or claim line in the TUI; changes to `next`, `handoff`, or `start`; new status colors.

## Why

The two queues are roles, not a list of status spellings. `config.in_work()` is already started plus reviewing when that role is set. `review_status` is the handoff queue, and `next --status review` already draws from it one item at a time. `list` can show the whole queue, but only if the caller repeats `--status` with the right keys. A project that renamed a label still has to pass the status key.

In-work means the status, not the claim. `release` clears the owner and leaves the item in progress, and that row still belongs in the queue (the list shows `*` in CLAIM). An item that is only started or claimed in a sibling worktree stays on the default list's CLAIM column and `in_work_elsewhere`. It is not in this checkout's in-work view.

## Failing tests

1. `--in-work` returns started items and, when `reviewing_status` is set, reviewing items. Open, review, parked, done, and retired items stay out. A started item with no claim owner still matches.
2. `--review` returns only `review_status`. Reviewing and started items stay out. The flag matches that configured key even when its label is not the word review.
3. `--in-work` together with `--review`, `--status`, or `--all` exits 2 with code `usage`. `--review` with `--status` or `--all` does the same.
4. `--review` when `review_status` is empty, and `--in-work` when `in_work()` is empty, exit 2 with code `usage`. A configured role that matches nothing prints `no matching items`, exits 0, and does not print the hidden-count line.
5. `--tree`, `--pass`, `--flag`, and `--sort` still narrow or order the chosen view. JSON stays an array of the same item objects.
6. In the TUI, `v` cycles the status preset from the initial unfinished set, to in-work, to review, and back to that unfinished set. Search and the other filters stay. A custom status selection counts as the unfinished stop, so the first `v` selects in-work and the return stop is the initial unfinished set, not the custom selection.
7. The status line shows `view=in-work` or `view=review` while that preset is active. `c`, and a jump that clears filters to reveal a hidden item, clear the preset. Applying the filter panel clears the preset and keeps the checked statuses.
8. When review is disabled, `v` skips that stop. When no in-work status is configured, `v` skips that stop. When both are unavailable, `v` does nothing and says so. `J` and `K` stay disabled while a preset is active.
9. The shortcut strip still occupies two rows at 80 columns and one row at 160, and `?` lists `v`.

## Implement

Add two flags on list: --in-work and --review. The words are fixed. --in-work keeps items whose status is in `config.in_work()`. --review keeps items whose status is `config.review_status`. Both replace the default of omitting done and retired, and both are mutually exclusive with --status, with --all, and with each other. Other list filters and sorts are unchanged. Text and JSON stay in their current shapes, including the CLAIM column for the rows that remain.

In the TUI, `v` cycles those two status sets around the initial unfinished set, as the tests describe. Store the preset by name so the status line can name it. Opening `f` shows the preset's statuses checked. Applying `f` drops the name. Put `v view` on the shortcut strip and in the help overlay.
